note: Small Clayton County Conservation park 3 mi north of Guttenberg on a Mississippi River backwater, with a boat ramp and shelter; free rough camping along a gravel lane between the railroad and the slough. Bare-bones, and closed when the river floods. --Claude
summary: Free camping confirmed (3 primitive sites, county page + facility page). Season May - October. Waterfront lead riverview -> not waterfront (tree belt between lane and duckweed backwater). Pin ~560 m off.
flags: WATERFRONT LEAD (riverview -> not waterfront, a downgrade; unsure after every source, so down): the camping is along a gravel lane on a narrow strip between the railroad and a Mississippi backwater. On NAIP (full leaf) and Esri a belt of trees 15-30 m deep stands between the lane and the slough everywhere a camper is parked, and the slough beside the park is duckweed-covered marsh with emergent vegetation; the open backwater is 150 m+ east. The county's 'Camp along the Mississippi River' is marketing and cannot be the basis. Overpass was down (imagery estimates).

PIN (~560 m off): stored 42.85200,-91.10600 is in the marsh north of the park; a camper is parked on the lane at about 42.8469,-91.1064, which is the camping strip. Google's pin 42.84522,-91.10719 is on Mississippi Rd at the entrance.

BOOKING unclear: MyCountyParks lists a 'Frenchtown Campground' facility with an availability calendar, but the page names no check-in time ('N/A') and no fee; whether it is booked there or first come is not stated. Stored reservable false / fcfs always (note prose) left as derived.
